rows.note: Bare filename: --list records file=null, and measure.py:171-193 resolves none of `dispositions.json`, corpus/knowledge/dispositions.json, corpus/dispositions.json, corpus/lessons/dispositions.json at base, so check_reads marks it unresolved (measure.py:271-279) unless a row claims `absent`. The target is not absent - the sentence means the round-14 after-manifest, which the lane holds at .ufo/evidence/round-14/dispositions.json (sha256 77faac58…): its producer_before row is `"state": "superseded"` (:36) with `raw_receipt`/`raw_check` kept (:38-39) and `superseded_by` naming producer_before_oracle + producer_after_oracle (:40-43), the two replacement rows being `state: effective` (:46-49 and :51-55). So only the file qualifier is missing. The excerpt above is quoted from that intended target (verified there), not from a file at the written path; fixed_excerpt is the same text. Scratch probe of the 28aeef4 archive copy: exit 0, counts effective=11 superseded=1, matching the sentence's `→ 0`.

proposed_fix.why: The token has no directory, so the frozen extractor resolves none of its four candidates and check_reads counts the pointer unresolved (measure.py:171-193,271-279); the lane does hold the manifest the sentence means at .ufo/evidence/round-14/dispositions.json (base blob sha256 77faac587f7c0c984d0d91a4096d3539467d422c15060b09f7c734c6d2809005). Qualifying the path keeps one path pointer: dry-running the frozen extractor on the edited section text yields 10 pointers before and after, ordinals 0-9 unchanged, and ordinal 4 then resolves to that file (was file=None). Section floor is 10 (measure.py FLOORS), so the pointer count and floor are untouched.
